failure.summary: vm.js reaches a single PC and loops forever with a wrapped-around stack pointer (sp=0x-40100058 at pc=0x43a254 for 100M ticks), so Doom never initialises and no frame is saved; the grader's `node /app/vm.js` times out waiting for /tmp/frame.bmp. The 2 h budget went into repeatedly regenerating vm.js and later chasing qemu-mipsel/gdb instead of fixing the 32-bit arithmetic that corrupts SP.

evidence_quotes.quote:
[VM] Entry=0x400110
[VM] Starting...
[VM] PC range: 0xc7a248 tk=26
[VM] Done ticks=26

candidates.why_relevant: Requires stating the first failing line and fixing it before rerunning; the reproducible symptom here (one PC, negative SP) was visible at step 265 and never treated as the error to fix, only rewritten around.
Card for repeated failures/hangs: bound commands, print loop progress, verify output before declaring success; the model printed progress but never used the stuck PC to isolate the bad instruction.

pending_relevant.why_relevant: Pending closed-plan card; if the acceptance artifact (/tmp/frame.bmp produced from a fresh `node /app/vm.js`) had been fixed up front, the 315 step exploration would have been anchored to one check.

skill_use.detail: Only the input-inspection card was opened, at step 0. The failure-repair and bounded-debug cards were never opened; the model's own diagnostics found the stuck PC and negative SP but it responded by regenerating the file again (e.g., steps 250, 255, 285, 305).

verdict.rationale: The emulator was close enough to run but repeatedly executed a single stuck instruction with a 32-bit-wrapped stack pointer, and the model preferred whole-file regeneration over isolating that one bug until the 7200 s timeout; no available skill covers MIPS emulation.
